note: Grounded repaint v3 2026-10-21: one vaulted cellar with a single flagstone floor; every figure stands or sits on the floor, a tub rim or a barrel at true scale (no shelves, nothing floating, adults only around the wine). Feminine words left of the vine pillar, masculine right. One box per item. Exits: stone stairs UP to the dining hall (top left), arched door and ramp up to the street (right, where the delivery van came in). The back tasting bar is the zoom spot. Champagne and cru moved to the tasting-bar zoom to keep the room uncrowded.

items.scene: A CALF (KAHV) naps on the straw at the foot of the stone steps down into the wine CELLAR.
A BOOT (boo-TEHY) is stuck upside down in the neck of a huge green BOTTLE standing on the cellar floor.
Same as English 'brasserie' (said brah-suh-REE): a waiter in a long white apron hurries his tray of shiny BRASS tankards up to the BRASSERIE.
Same as English 'appellation' (said ah-pay-lah-SYOHN): an old winemaker leans on his barrel and stamps a big red royal wax seal on his bottle: by decree, a wine of NAMED ORIGIN!
EVE RESTS (ee-VREHS) on the rim of the grape tub, purple-footed and swirly-eyed: the HEADY DIZZINESS of too much grape-stomping.
At the little TASTING table a goat sniffs glass after glass, unsure whether to be DISGUSTED (day-GEWS-) or delighted.
Same as English 'capsule' (said kahp-SEWL): a squirrel wears a shiny bottle CAP as a helmet while hugging his acorn: CAP-sule!
Same as English 'vodka' but stressed at the end, vod-KAH: a crow perched on the ice bucket croaks 'KAH!' at the frosty VODKA bottle chilling inside.
A TEENY gnome (VEENY) stands at the foot of a stone pillar wrapped in a curling grape VINE heavy with purple bunches.
Like English 'alcohol', said ahl-KOL: a glass of wine in tiny sunglasses looks so al-COOL on its barrel.
A ghost shouts 'BOO!' (boo-SHOHN) as he heaves a giant CORK over his head.
A woman balances a GLASS of red wine on her head and shrugs 'WHERE?' (VEHR): it is right on top of her!
A delivery VAN (VAN) backs into the cellar with its doors open, packed with crates of WINE.
A cellar hand yells 'TOE! NO!' (toh-NOH) as a runaway BARREL rolls right over his foot.
